current_row.boundary_rationale: This span opens immediately after the book’s own colophon closes the preceding frame, עַד הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.51.64, byte tier), “Thus far are the words of Jeremiah” (web:Jer.51.64) — the tier-1 signal standing at this seam, alongside the regnal age-at-accession formula that opens the appendix on Zedekiah’s own reign: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַחַ֤ת שָׁנָה֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ חמיטל חֲמוּטַ֥ל בַּֽת יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִלִּבְנָֽה (oshb:Jer.52.1, byte; a ketiv/qere pair sits over the mother’s name here, detailed below), matching “Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign. He reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.” (web:Jer.52.1). A regnal evaluation follows in its own verse, וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוֹיָקִֽים (oshb:Jer.52.2, byte) — “He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.” (web:Jer.52.2) — before the span closes on the rebellion report that sets the chapter’s crisis in motion, כִּ֣י עַל אַ֣ף יְהוָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה עַד הִשְׁלִיכ֥וֹ אוֹתָ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל, matching “For through Yahweh’s anger this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out from his presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.” (web:Jer.52.3). A paseq stands in this closing verse, oshb:Jer.52.3 (single-witness WLC; seg layer; a bare count, position not recorded). No fresh dating notice interrupts the chain from the accession formula to the rebellion report, so the three verses stay one span.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this opening span through the siege's dated onset that follows was rejected because the accession formula, the regnal evaluation, and the rebellion report form a closed backstory unit before any fresh dated action begins.

current_row.device_notes: A setumah closes the preceding frame at oshb:Jer.51.64 (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak corroboration under the Prophets addendum; not a driver here, absence never counterevidence). The queen mother’s name carries a ketiv/qere pair at oshb:Jer.52.1 (single-witness WLC): the consonantal text reads חמיטל where the received reading is חֲמוּטַ֥ל, the two forms differing in the letter standing for the name’s internal vowel. Zedekiah’s name recurs in the long tsidqiyahu spelling six times across this chapter (sweep: 6 verses), and in this span it stands twice, at oshb:Jer.52.1 and oshb:Jer.52.3, rather than the short tsidqiyah form the book attests elsewhere. The regnal evaluation measures Zedekiah against a named predecessor rather than a general standard, a comparison this chapter’s own bytes do not repeat for him.

Two further entries continue under that same clause, the second supplying the set's own total, בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שָׁלֹ֣שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִים֮ לִנְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֒ הֶגְלָ֗ה נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָן֙ רַב טַבָּחִ֔ים יְהוּדִ֕ים נֶ֕פֶשׁ שְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אַרְבָּעִ֣ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑ה כָּל נֶ֕פֶשׁ אַרְבַּ֥עַת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.52.30, byte), matching “in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty-five people. All the people numbered four thousand six hundred.” (web:Jer.52.30). A petuchah closes this span at oshb:Jer.52.30 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum), standing at the point where the summed total is given.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the three dated entries as three separate spans was considered, since three separate year notices sit inside these verses; it is rejected because one governing clause introduces the three figures and the closing total sums them into one accounting rather than three independent notices.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A verse-initial date frame opens this span reckoned on an entirely different chronology from the totals just given: thirty-seven years to the exile of the king of Judah, וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ן מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte tier). A second, mid-verse date element follows on the Babylonian side, בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מַלְכֻת֗וֹ (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte tier), “in his reign” — a reign-year phrase carrying no ordinal token in the Hebrew; the “first year” of the English rendering, “Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and released him from prison.” (web:Jer.52.31), is the rendering's own supplement rather than a byte fact. The verse in full reads וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ן מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה בִּשְׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ חֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ נָשָׂ֡א אֱוִ֣יל מְרֹדַךְ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֜ל בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מַלְכֻת֗וֹ אֶת רֹאשׁ֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיֹּצֵ֥א אוֹת֖וֹ מִבֵּ֥ית הכליא הַכְּלֽוּא (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte; this verse also carries a ketiv/qere pair and two spellings of Jehoiachin's own name, both detailed below), so the onset in fact carries two date elements rather than one. A petuchah closes the preceding census entries at oshb:Jer.52.30 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum), immediately before this dated notice opens a fresh scene in Babylon. The span continues through the king's changed provision, closing on its own standing arrangement, וַאֲרֻחָת֗וֹ אֲרֻחַת֩ תָּמִ֨יד נִתְּנָה לּ֜וֹ מֵאֵ֧ת מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֛ל דְּבַר י֥וֹם בְּיוֹמ֖וֹ עַד י֣וֹם מוֹת֑וֹ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו (oshb:Jer.52.34, byte), matching “For his allowance, there was a continual allowance given him by the king of Babylon, every day a portion until the day of his death, all the days of his life.” (web:Jer.52.34).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this release notice into the preceding chronicle of deportation totals was rejected because a fresh verse-initial dated frame on a different reckoning, reckoned to the exile of the king of Judah rather than to Nebuchadnezzar's regnal years, opens a distinct scene in Babylon rather than continuing the count.
current_row.literature_type_guess: dated notice of a royal captive's release and provision
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: This verse carries two date elements, not one: the verse-initial exile-year reckoning and a separate mid-verse Babylonian reign-year phrase carrying no ordinal of its own. Jehoiachin's name is spelled two ways within this span's opening verse, oshb:Jer.52.31 (byte): the dating clause reads יְהוֹיָכִ֣ן, without the internal letter the narrative clause supplies two clauses later in the same verse, יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין, naming the head that is lifted up. Both spellings render the yehoyakhin name form, one of the king's three name forms across the book, and neither is the Jeconiah or Coniah form attested elsewhere. A ketiv/qere pair also stands in this verse over the word for his confinement (single-witness WLC): the consonantal text reads הכליא where the received reading is הַכְּלֽוּא. A further ketiv/qere pair stands at oshb:Jer.52.32 over the word for the other kings with him in Babylon: the consonantal text reads מלכים where the received reading is הַמְּלָכִ֛ים, the received form supplying the definite article the consonantal text leaves without.
